tables.title: Arthurian Britain Ruin Types
values: A city once inhabited by not-quite-humans — giants, fair folk, or pre-Celtic peoples
A Roman structure whose purpose is no longer clear — bath-house, amphitheatre, granary
A spot that was once a sacred site of the old religion
A vast monument complex — stone circle, cursus, long barrow — dedicated to a vanished people
Fortress raised by a dead warlord, failed king, or militant faith
A sorcerer's tower or hermit's compound once or presently inhabited by a powerful figure
Roll twice on 1d6 above; the first result was built on top of or in the ruins of the second
Roll again, but now inhabited by bandits, exiles, Saxon refugees, or other interlopers
A Roman road-fort whose garrison has been replaced by something worse
A barrow complex — multiple burial chambers, several generations of the honoured dead
A working or partly-working Roman relic — mill, aqueduct, dock — now badly decayed
A former estate or villa, gutted and half-collapsed, but recognisable

tables.title: General Places of Adventure
values: A lost temple to a dead or forbidden god
Ruins of a Roman town or fortified settlement
Cavernous tunnels — old mine workings, natural caves, or barrow galleries
Ruined fortress of a former warlord or Roman garrison
Town ruins swept away by plague, fire, or Saxon raid
Lair of a legendary beast or monster
Sorcerer's tower or abandoned scholars' complex
A place of confinement built to hold a dangerous power
Pilgrimage site for a lost or persecuted religion
A nexus of faerie or otherworldly power
Mortuary complex — barrow, cairn-field, or Roman mausoleum — for a lost people
Stronghold of exiles, rebels, or Saxon newcomers
A settlement or den of dangerous inhuman folk
An underground settlement — carved hillfort, worked cave-complex, collapsed mine
An abandoned pleasure-place of a former lord — hunting lodge, baths, summer villa
Sinister ruined estate of a former lord
Roll again; now inhabited by interlopers
Roll twice; one built on top of the other

tables.title: Wilderness Encounters — Human
values: Hermit with a good reason to stay alone
Peasant perhaps moonlighting as a bandit
Patrol of the local lord's men
Miners, woodsmen, hunters, or other workers
Noble or gentry on a journey
Pilgrim, perhaps of a malevolent or pagan god

tables.title: Wilderness Encounters — Nonhuman or Faerie
values: Raiders on their way to pillage a site
Patrol to drive off troublesome intruders
Site of a bloody battle with nonhumans

tables.title: Wilderness Encounters — Beasts and Monsters
values: Stalking predator looking for an opening
An ambush predator lying in wait
Ghost, animate corpse, or other undead
Something far too dangerous to confront directly

tables.title: Wilderness Encounters — What Is Happening (With Sapients)
values: Examining recent loot or a finding
Need healing or help with a situation
In an affable and friendly mood

tables.title: Wilderness Encounters — What Is Happening (With Beasts)
values: Remnants of its last prey are nearby
Using bait to lure in humans
Old or crippled and acting unpredictably
